narrative.overview:
A passage through a gate into a room of paper and wood. Black lacquer frames every region, cool washi paper carries the words, dark grained wood holds what is shelved or rolled, and beyond the gate is a velvet black lit only by taking darkness away. One vermilion cord runs through the system: the control at the gate, the line Experience and Technologies hang from, and the colour of everything a visitor can act on. Everything else is ghosted grey until struck.

Density is low and deliberate: large type, tall sections, one thing at a time (the gate and its verse, one pulled-forward book, one portrait). The gate is locked until the visitor pulls the cord, pushes down, drags the scrollbar or follows a tab; then a timed opening plays. Motion is heavy and decisive, like weighted wood. Bleach is evoked through original material (gate, paper, lacquer, cord, hanko seal, ink butterflies), never borrowed artwork.
keyCharacteristics: four materials (lacquer, washi, grained wood, void)
three type voices (display gothic, Mincho for what is written or spoken on paper, quiet gothic for UI and prose)
square surfaces (rounding only on turned wood and the focus ring)
texture from two tiling SVG grains, never images
light and focus conveyed by removing darkness

rules.name: The One Cord Rule
rules.body: Vermilion marks the cord and what hangs from it, what can be acted on, and the owner's red ink (seal, stamps). It never decorates headings, fills sections or tints imagery.

rules.name: The Removal of Darkness Rule
rules.body: Focus and arrival lift a shade (unchosen books dimmed to 55%, the passage flooding with seam light), not add colour or brightness.

rules.name: The Cool Paper Rule
rules.body: Paper is cool washi; browns only age its edges.

rules.name: The Spoken Line Rule
rules.body: Mincho is for lines written or voiced on paper. It never sets UI, labels or buttons.

rules.name: The Numbered Registry Rule
rules.body: Destinations and volumes carry two-digit display numerals; the number is part of the name.

rules.name: The Label Is Data Rule
rules.body: Uppercase tracked labels name a field, status, group or destination. Never an eyebrow above a heading.

rules.name: The Planes Not Cards Rule
rules.body: Elevation is one material in front of another. No generic card shadows.

rules.name: The Two Grains Rule
rules.body: Paper takes the paper grain, wood the wood grain, nothing else is textured; never over text-bearing vermilion or void.

dos: **Do** frame every region in lacquer, put words meant to be read slowly on washi, and shelve or roll things on grained wood.
**Do** keep vermilion to the cord, controls, links, focus and the owner's red ink; Lit Vermilion on black, Deep Vermilion on paper.

**Do** give every link and button a hover animation, never a colour change alone, from the page's vocabulary: a red stroke cuts in or a seam opens under it; it strikes forward; it lifts and red rises from its foot; or its mark turns. Keyboard focus gets the same answer. Movement runs only with a real pointer and motion allowed; colour still changes under reduced motion. Entrances ease out over 0.25-0.35s, exits are quicker, a press sinks the control.
**Do** show focus or arrival by lifting darkness rather than adding colour, with a non-colour cue (underline) wherever colour marks the chosen item.

**Do** number destinations and volumes with two-digit display numerals; apply the grain tokens to the right material; write any new type size as a clamp() on `calc(N * var(--fluid))`, never raw vw, so it follows browser zoom.
**Do** honour reduced motion: the gate stays whole, the page is unlocked, and nothing parts, swings, draws, unrolls or moves in the wind.
**Do** keep every interactive target at least 44px tall, and never let a theme change animate hover states.
donts: **Don't** warm the paper toward cream, add a second accent, or use vermilion on headings or section backgrounds.
**Don't** round surfaces or controls beyond the focus ring, door pulls.
**Don't** set UI, buttons or labels in Mincho, or place tracked labels above headings.
**Don't** use official Bleach artwork, logos, characters or quoted text; everything drawn is original.
**Don't** use images or photography for texture, or bouncy and elastic easing for state changes.
